findings.title: Inline getUser() census omits app/(dashboard)/agents/[id]/actions.ts; real totals are 72/29 and 57/18
findings.where: Residual gap; Enforcement layer 3 (opening); Requirements deviations 1; Bypass analysis row '45 calls, 17 files'; Backlog 1; response-log NIT 5
findings.problem: The 17-file enumeration omits app/(dashboard)/agents/[id]/actions.ts, which holds 12 inline auth.getUser() calls (lines 59, 109, 323, 371, 408, 458, 544, 603, 627, 752, 834, 861). Counted with -LiteralPath over app/ + lib/ excluding *.test.*, the repo has 72 calls across 29 non-test files, not 60/28, and the inline-action subset is 57 calls across 18 files, not 45/17. Cause: a search that silently treats [id] as a character class and drops bracketed dynamic-route directories (reproducing exactly 60/28). This is the inventory that defines the residual security gap and scopes backlog item 1, and the design asserts it as personally verified against two earlier counts.
findings.fix: Restate as '72 auth.getUser( call sites across 29 non-test files; getCurrentOrgAndUser backs 16; 57 inline calls across 18 action files', add 'agents/[id]/actions.ts 12' to the per-file enumeration, update the bypass-analysis row to (57 calls, 18 files), and note in backlog 1 that requireOrgContext() must cover agent CRUD and voice-save paths. Re-count with -LiteralPath so [id] directories are not skipped.

findings.title: fd_mfa_attempts 'secure when https' has no specified source in a server action, and getting it wrong silently disables the attempt bound
findings.problem: lib/auth/recovery.ts exports only the cookie name and max-age; the attribute set being copied lives in app/(auth)/callback/route.ts and derives secure from request.nextUrl.protocol. bumpFailedAttempts() takes no arguments and runs in a server action with no NextRequest, so 'secure when https' has no source and at least three readings. If an implementer picks secure: true, the browser drops the cookie on http://localhost, the counter always reads 0, the five-failure sign-out never fires, and AC10's second half cannot be demonstrated in dev while the mocked unit test still passes.
findings.fix: Declare MFA_ATTEMPTS_COOKIE_OPTIONS in lib/auth/mfa.ts next to the other constants with httpOnly: true, sameSite: 'lax', secure: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production', path: '/', maxAge: MFA_ATTEMPTS_MAX_AGE_SECONDS, use it from both helpers, and state that the callback keeps its request-derived secure for fd_password_recovery because no request object is in scope in an action.

findings.title: proxy.test.ts and callback/route.test.ts have no specified Vitest environment; no repo precedent for NextRequest under jsdom
findings.where: Testability (proxy.test.ts mocking and NextRequest construction); Files touched row for app/(auth)/callback/route.test.ts
findings.problem: vitest.config.ts sets environment: 'jsdom' globally with no override and is out of scope for this run. No existing test file in the repo imports NextRequest, NextResponse, or next/experimental/testing/server, so these are the first Next server primitives exercised under a DOM global environment (jsdom supplies no fetch/Request/Response/Headers; those survive only by inheritance from Node's undici). AC5/AC6/AC8/AC12 evidence depends on these two files running, and the design otherwise specifies mock shapes, ordinal assertions, and helper naming in detail.
findings.fix: Specify a '// @vitest-environment node' docblock at the top of proxy.test.ts and app/(auth)/callback/route.test.ts in both the Testability section and the Files touched rows; lib/auth/mfa.test.ts, app/(auth)/actions.test.ts, lib/data/organization.test.ts and lib/validations/auth.test.ts stay on jsdom.

findings.title: Layer-3 insertion snippet returns [] for three functions whose return type is not an array
findings.problem: The table lists the correct return shapes but the single snippet shows 'return []' for all ten functions. getConversationNavCounts returns { unreadConversations, unreadMessages } (with a local 'empty' at lib/data/conversations.ts:155 inside a try), getConversationById returns Conversation | null, and getConversationRecordingUrl returns string | null. Copying the snippet literally is a tsc failure under NFR 27.
findings.fix: Replace the single snippet with three: 'return []' for clients/integrations/phone-numbers/staff/sidebar-preferences/getConversationsForOrg, 'return empty' for getConversationNavCounts (inside the existing try), and 'return null' for getConversationById and getConversationRecordingUrl.

findings.title: getCurrentOrgAndUser consumer census is 16 sites in 16 files, not 15/15
findings.where: Enforcement layer 2, 'Verified consumer list (15 call sites, 15 files)'; response-log NIT 5
findings.problem: app/(dashboard)/agents/[id]/page.tsx:20 is missing — the same bracketed-path blind spot as finding 1. The conclusion is unaffected (that page also does 'if (!context) redirect("/login")'), but that route calls getAgentById(id) and notFound() at line 19 before the layer-2 gate at line 20, so 'layer 2 gates before any protected read' is not literally true there.

findings.title: pattern={REGEXP_ONLY_DIGITS} is forwarded to the real input; the stated mechanism is wrong
findings.where: The verify form ('it is not forwarded to the <input> as an HTML attribute'); response-log NIT 11
findings.problem: input-otp@1.4.2's dist/index.mjs destructures pattern out of props and re-applies it to the rendered input as 'pattern: m?.source', so the real <input> carries pattern="^\d+$". Harmless and the delivered behavior is unchanged, but an implementer who sees the attribute in devtools after reading 'not forwarded' will go looking for a bug. The adjacent claims are verified: autoComplete defaults to one-time-code in the library, and id/inputMode/disabled/autoFocus/aria-* are spread onto the input.
findings.fix: Reword to: pattern is consumed by input-otp, compiled into an internal RegExp that rejects non-digit keystrokes and pastes, and also re-emitted on the real input as pattern="^\d+$" (regexp.source); the keystroke filtering, not the HTML attribute, is what this design relies on.

findings.title: /llms.txt is a real public asset the matcher catches and the allowlist misses
findings.problem: public/llms.txt exists and is served at /llms.txt. config.matcher excludes only _next/static, _next/image, favicon.ico and the image extensions, so a pending-MFA session gets a 307 to /verify for it. Negligible impact, but the list is explicitly exhaustive about /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml and /manifest.webmanifest, and the rest of public/ is .svg/.png and already matcher-excluded.
findings.fix: Add '/llms.txt' to MFA_EXEMPT_PREFIXES, or state that it is deliberately gated.

findings.title: endPendingSession's signOut() failure is unspecified, leaving a hole in the never-rejects posture
findings.where: The verify and cancel actions (endPendingSession signature); Error handling summary
findings.problem: lib/auth/mfa.ts is contractually rejection-free, but endPendingSession lives in app/(auth)/actions.ts and calls supabase.auth.signOut(), which rethrows non-AuthErrors. A rejection means the redirect is never reached, so the declared Promise<never> becomes a rejected promise: the user stays pending with no copy, on the one escape path a stuck user has.
findings.fix: Specify the body with try { await supabase.auth.signOut() } catch { /* best effort; the redirect still strips the user from the app and the gate keeps denying */ } before clearFailedAttempts() and the redirect, and add the row to the error-handling table. The existing logOut ignores the signOut result too, so this matches house style.

findings.title: 'PendingSessionEndReason is a subset of this map's keys, so the two cannot drift' is unenforced
findings.where: login/page.tsx notices, after the LOGIN_NOTICES literal
findings.problem: LOGIN_NOTICES lives in app/(auth)/login/page.tsx and PendingSessionEndReason in app/(auth)/actions.ts with no reference between them, so nothing makes the subset relation a typecheck error. Adding a reason and forgetting the notice yields a silently invisible message — the exact problem this section exists to fix.
findings.fix: Export PendingSessionEndReason, define LoginNoticeCode = PendingSessionEndReason | 'session_expired' | 'missing_code' | 'oauth_failed' | 'org_setup_failed' in login/page.tsx, and declare LOGIN_NOTICES with 'satisfies Record<LoginNoticeCode, { tone: "danger" | "neutral"; text: string }>'.

verified_assumptions: auth-js 2.112.2: the no-argument _getAuthenticatorAssuranceLevel branch derives nextLevel from cookie-stored session.user.factors, is not wrapped in try/catch (only the jwt branch is), and dereferences session.user.factors and decodeJWT(session.access_token) unguarded — the threat model and the load-bearing try/catch are both correct.
auth-js decodeJWT (lib/helpers.js:177) performs no signature verification; the design's ordering-dependency argument for trusting payload.aal is accurate.
getUser() has no local-JWKS or caching shortcut: the public method delegates to _getUser(), which always requests GET /user with the session access token, and rethrows non-AuthErrors.

_listFactors calls getUser() then user?.factors ?? [], and buckets on status === 'verified' with no factor-type filter (plus a webauthn bucket) — step 2's verified-only test and backlog 7 are justified.
With no session the AAL call returns { currentLevel: null, nextLevel: null } with error: null, so the null-to-pending mapping is what closes that case.
All nine error.code values in the mapping table exist in auth-js's ErrorCode union.

@supabase/ssr 0.12.4 SetAllCookies takes (cookies, headers); the CDN-caching doc comment and the three header values are verbatim; CookieOptions is re-exported from the package root; docker/nginx.conf exists.

The existing config.matcher reaches every page navigation, RSC payload and action POST, and does not match /_next/static/chunk.js.

wrong_assumptions: '60 call sites across 28 non-test files' and '45 calls across 17 files' — actually 72/29 and 57/18 (finding 1).
'Verified consumer list (15 call sites, 15 files)' for getCurrentOrgAndUser — actually 16/16 (finding 5).
'pattern ... is not forwarded to the <input> as an HTML attribute' — it is, as regexp.source (finding 6).
The proxy.md quote is paraphrased and :249/:251 are :248/:250 (finding 7).

'The headers parameter is mandatory in @supabase/ssr's SetAllCookies type' — the parameter is declared, but TypeScript permits a one-parameter implementation, so the type does not force a caller to accept it.

'following the fd_password_recovery precedent in lib/auth/recovery.ts (httpOnly, sameSite lax, secure when https ...)' — that module holds only the name and max-age; the attributes live in callback/route.ts (finding 2).
unverified_assumptions: That this Supabase project emits aal/aal2 claims and issues OAuth sessions at aal1 (manual; fails closed if absent).

That GoTrue /user returns factors for an aal1 session — never stated as an assumption by the design, and the gate fails OPEN if false. Strongly supported by getTotpFactorStatus shipping on the same read; should be added to the manual verification list explicitly.
That mfa.verify()'s refreshed aal2 cookies survive a real server-action round trip.
NFR 26's no-measurable-regression claim (the static half checks out: the proxy's getUser is replaced not added, and layers 2-3 add only a storage-local AAL read).
The real test baseline (AGENTS.md says 3 files, the requirements say 10 failures across 4).
Whether NextRequest/NextResponse behave under the global jsdom environment (finding 3).
Whether concurrent runs have rewritten the layer-3 helpers or created app/(dashboard)/analytics/actions.test.ts — the tree was clean when read, so nothing has landed yet.
